assignedReviews.card_evidence: Jogging and other regular exercise strengthen your heart and muscles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that exercise strengthens the heart and muscles but does not describe how the muscular or circulatory systems work, which is the action required by the competency.

copy.en: Jogging and other regular exercise strengthen your heart and muscles, keeping your body healthy and full of energy!
copy.tl: Ang regular na ehersisyo gaya ng jogging ay nagpapalakas ng puso at kalamnan, at tumutulong para manatiling malusog at masigla ang katawan!
copy.bis: Ang regular nga ehersisyo sama sa jogging makapalig-on sa kasingkasing ug kaunoran, ug makatabang aron magpabiling himsog ug kusgan ang lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the awesome unit we use to measure energy or work
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines the joule as a unit for energy or work. It does not teach that energy can cause change, nor does it mention light, sound, or heat energy, which are the focus of G4-F-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the awesome unit we use to measure energy or work
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that work is done when a force causes the displacement of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions work only as something measured in joules. It does not explain that work is done when a force causes displacement, which is the core concept of G8-F-6.

copy.en: Meet the joule (J)! It is the awesome unit we use to measure energy or work.
copy.tl: Kilalanin ang joule (J)! Ito ang yunit na ginagamit natin para sumukat ng energy o work.
copy.bis: Ilha ang joule (J)! Kini mao ang unit nga atong gigamit aron sukdon ang energy o work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Juno probe explores the planet Jupiter!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the Juno probe explores Jupiter, the biggest planet. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, identify major celestial objects, their main features, or composition, which is the focus of G5-E-11.

copy.en:
Which probe explores the biggest planet in our solar system?

The Juno probe explores the planet Jupiter! It is busy studying the biggest planet of all.
copy.tl:
Aling probe ang gumagalugad sa pinakamalaking planeta sa ating solar system?

Ang Juno probe ang gumagalugad sa planetang Jupiter! Masipag itong nag-aaral sa pinakamalaking planeta.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga probe ang nagasuhid sa pinakadako nga planeta sa atong solar system?

Ang Juno probe ang nagasuhid sa planeta nga Jupiter! Kugihan kini nga nagtuon sa pinakadako nga planeta.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about Jupiter's rotation speed, but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, the names of major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition. It only touches on one feature of one planet.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about demonstrating the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night. The card is about Jupiter's spin, not Earth's rotation, and does not address day and night or use a globe.

copy.en:
Which planet is the fastest-spinning in our solar system?

Jupiter is the fastest-spinning planet! It completes one whole turn in only about 10 hours.
copy.tl:
Aling planeta ang pinakamabilis umikot sa ating solar system?

Jupiter ang pinakamabilis umikot na planeta! Kumpleto ang isang ikot nito sa halos 10 hours lang.
copy.bis:
Asa nga planeta ang pinakapaspas motuyok sa atong solar system?

Jupiter ang pinakapaspas motuyok nga planeta! Makompleto ang usa ka tibuok tuyok sa mga 10 hours lang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Jupiter's four biggest moons are Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names four moons of Jupiter. The competency requires describing the general structure of the solar system, including main features and composition of major celestial objects. Naming moons is a minor vocabulary overlap, not direct instructional support for the competency's substantive content.

copy.en: Jupiter's four biggest moons are Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.
copy.tl: Ang apat na pinakamalaking buwan ng Jupiter ay sina Io, Europa, Ganymede, at Callisto.
copy.bis: Ang upat ka pinakadako nga bulan sa Jupiter mao sila Io, Europa, Ganymede, ug Callisto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Jupiter is so massive it weighs more than all seven other planets combined!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about Jupiter's mass relative to other planets. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, nor does it identify the names of major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition beyond this one comparative statement. The fact is related to the solar system topic but does not directly support the competency's required description.

copy.en: Jupiter is so massive it weighs more than all seven other planets combined! That makes it the true 'king' of size and mass in our solar system.
copy.tl: Sobrang bigat ng Jupiter, mas mabigat pa kaysa sa pitong planeta na pinagsama-sama! Kaya siya talaga ang 'hari' ng laki at bigat sa ating solar system.
copy.bis: Bug-at kaayo ang Jupiter, mas bug-at pa kaysa sa pito ka planeta nga gisagol! Mao nga kini gyud ang 'hari' sa kadako ug kabug-at sa atong solar system.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires identifying gravity as a non-contact force affecting objects on Earth. The card discusses Jupiter's gravity, not Earth's, and does not address the non-contact nature or Earth-specific predictable behaviors. It shares the topic of gravity but provides no direct instructional support for the Earth-focused competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you’d feel more than twice as heavy as on Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to observe and describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. The card describes a hypothetical weight change on Jupiter, not the motion of an object under gravity, and does not involve observation or description of motion. It is only related to gravity as a general concept.

copy.en:
How heavy would you feel on Jupiter?

Jupiter’s massive gravity pulls hard! If you could stand there, you’d feel more than twice as heavy as on Earth, like carrying a big backpack!
copy.tl:
Gaano ka kabigat sa Jupiter?

Napakalakas ng gravity ng Jupiter! Kung makatayo ka roon, magiging mahigit doble ang bigat mo kaysa sa Earth, parang may dala kang malaking backpack!
copy.bis:
Unsa kabug-at nimo sa Jupiter?

Kusog kaayo ang gravity sa Jupiter! Kung makatindog ka didto, mahimong sobra sa doble ang imong gibug-aton kaysa sa Earth, morag nagdala ka og dako nga backpack!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Jupiter! It has more than 90 moons — just behind Saturn, the moon champion!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a specific trivia fact about the number of moons of Jupiter and Saturn. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, nor does it identify the names of major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition in a way that directly supports the competency. It is only tangentially related to the solar system topic.

copy.en:
Which planet has the second most moons in our solar system?

Jupiter! It has more than 90 moons — just behind Saturn, the moon champion!
copy.tl:
Aling planeta ang may pangalawa sa pinakamaraming buwan sa ating solar system?

Jupiter! Mayroon itong mahigit 90 na buwan — sumunod lang sa Saturn, ang champion ng mga buwan!
copy.bis:
Asang planeta ang adunay ikaduha sa labing daghang bulan sa atong solar system?

Jupiter! Adunay kini kapin sa 90 ka bulan — sunod lang sa Saturn, ang champion sa mga bulan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A Great Conjunction happens when Jupiter and Saturn look super close
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Jupiter and Saturn as celestial objects but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, their main features, or composition. It only notes their apparent closeness during a conjunction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A Great Conjunction happens when Jupiter and Saturn look super close
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a conjunction of planets but does not address how or when the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars move across the sky. It provides no instructional support for observing or recording celestial motion.

copy.en: A Great Conjunction happens when Jupiter and Saturn look super close, about every 20 years! In December 2020, they were closest in 400 years, looking like one bright star!
copy.tl: Ang Great Conjunction ay nangyayari kapag magkalapit ang Jupiter at Saturn, mga bawat 20 taon! Noong Disyembre 2020, sila ang pinakamagkalapit sa 400 taon, tila isang maliwanag na bituin!
copy.bis: Ang Great Conjunction mahitabo sa dihang magkaduol ang Jupiter ug Saturn, mga matag 20 ka tuig! Niadtong Disyembre 2020, sila ang pinakaduol sa 400 ka tuig, morag usa ka hayag nga bituin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: prefers to glide through the air instead
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the kagwang's current behavior (clumsy on ground, slow climbing, preference for gliding) but does not describe how the animal has changed over time to suit its environment, nor does it use secondary sources. Gliding is an adaptation, but the competency specifically asks for examples of animals that have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage; this card only states a present-day trait without evolutionary change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: prefers to glide through the air instead
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gliding through the air, which relates to an aerial mode of movement, but it does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat, and it does not explicitly classify the kagwang as terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial. The format-required activity (drawing/diagram classification) is absent, so this is at most related_only.

copy.en: The kagwang is clumsy on the ground and climbs very slowly — that's why it prefers to glide through the air instead.
copy.tl: Mahina ang kagwang sa paglakad sa lupa at mabagal itong umakyat — kaya mas gusto nitong gumliid sa hangin.
copy.bis: Luya ang kagwang molakaw sa yuta ug hinay mosaka — mao nga mas gusto niini ang pagliid sa hangin.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the structure of a compound leaf (many leaflets on one stalk) but does not address the role of leaves, roots, or stems in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the focus of G3-L-5. It shares the topic 'leaves' but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's stated skill.

copy.en:
What is a compound leaf?

The kakawate's leaf is a compound leaf — it's made up of many small leaflets attached to just one stalk.
copy.tl:
Ano ang compound leaf?

Ang dahon ng kakawate ay tinatawag na compound leaf dahil binubuo ito ng maraming maliliit na dahon sa iisang tangkay.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang compound leaf?

Ang dahon sa kakawate gitawag og compound leaf tungod kay gilangkoban kini sa daghang gagmay nga dahon sa usa ka tangkay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its loud call can be heard right at dawn and dusk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a loud call that can be heard, which touches on sound and hearing, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred. It is an animal behavior fact, not instruction on sound production or transmission.

copy.en:
Why is the kalaw called the 'clock of the mountains'?

The kalaw is called the 'clock of the mountains' because its loud call can be heard right at dawn and dusk — almost like it's announcing the time!
copy.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na 'relo ng bundok' ang kalaw?

Tinatawag na 'relo ng bundok' ang kalaw dahil naririnig ang malakas nitong tawag sa umaga at gabi — parang nagpapaalam ito ng oras!
copy.bis:
Ngano gitawag nga 'relo sa bundok' ang kalaw?

Gitawag nga 'relo sa bundok' ang kalaw tungod kay ang iyang kusog nga tawag mabati sa kaagahon ug kagabhion — daw nagpahibalo kini sa oras!
